data.description:
## Context / Problem

After the reducer child, rebar can store `releases` but the bridge never reads Jira's `fixVersions`: the Cloud search requests a fixed field list without it (`src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:238-251`), no inbound differ compares it, and no applier writes it. So a fix version a team sets in Jira never reaches the bound rebar ticket. This child implements the Jira→rebar direction designed in ADR 0123 (decisions 3, 4 and 7), following the labels→tags path.

## Approach

1. **Fetch.** Add `"fixVersions"` to the Cloud search field list in `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py` (lines 241-250). The Data Center adapter needs no fetch change: its `search_issues` passes no `fields` argument to pycontribs (`src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:199-205`, called page by page from `fetch_paging.py:91`), and pycontribs `JIRA.search_issues` maps an omitted or `None` `fields` to `["*all"]` (pycontribs/jira `jira/client.py`, `search_issues`); the DC test below pins that `fixVersions` survives `_unwrap`. The bound-but-absent direct GET (`get_issue_by_rest`, `acli_rest.py:325-333`) already returns all fields.
2. **Diff.** Add `_diff_releases_inbound(jira_fields, local_ticket)` to `src/rebar/reconciler/inbound_collection_diffs.py` beside `_diff_labels_inbound` (lines 194-214). It reads the names from `jira_fields["fixVersions"]` (a list of version objects; take each dict's `name`, skip entries without a string name), set-diffs them against `local_ticket["releases"]`, and returns sorted `{"action": "add"|"remove", "release": name}` records. Observation guard: when `"fixVersions"` is absent from `jira_fields`, or is not a list, return `[]`, so a snapshot that never fetched the field cannot be read as "all releases removed". This mirrors the G1 guard in `_diff_link_removals_inbound` (same file, lines 168-172).
3. **Mutation.** Add a `releases` list field to `InboundMutation` (`src/rebar/reconciler/inbound_differ.py:60-70`), compute it in `compute_inbound_mutations` (line 289 onward), and include it in the emit condition (line 353). To keep `compute_inbound_mutations` within its complexity ceiling, first extract the existing label-suppression block (lines 308-322) into a behavior-preserving helper `_suppress_collection_echoes(mutations, adds, removes, key)`; the outbound child reuses it for releases. Carry `"releases"` through `run_differs.py` (the inbound typed-payload dict at lines 365-380) and add it to `InboundUpdatePayload` and `_INBOUND_UPDATE_KEYS` in `src/rebar/reconciler/mutation_payloads.py` (lines 264-301).
4. **Apply.** In `src/rebar/reconciler/apply_inbound_events.py`, extract the read-state/no-op-suppression/add-wins-dedup body of `_inbound_update_apply_labels` (lines 322-389) into a shared `_apply_inbound_list_delta(...)` parameterized by payload key, entry key, state key and event type, and call it for labels (`TAG_DELTA`, unchanged behavior) and for releases (`RELEASE_DELTA`). Both write `source="inbound"` and both skip the write when the reducer fails or returns `None`. Call the release applier from `apply_inbound.py` next to the labels call (line 133).
5. **Contract.** Register `"releases": FieldSymmetry(name="releases", symmetry=ADD_WINS, conflict_class="set", outbound_name="fixVersions", codec="Jira fixVersions[].name ↔ local 'releases'", notes=...)` in `src/rebar/reconciler/_field_contract.py`, and `"releases": "set"` in `conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES` (`src/rebar/reconciler/conflict_resolver.py:28-39`). The import-time guard in `tests/unit/reconciler/test_field_contract_properties.py:32-52` then covers it.
6. **Docs.** Add a "Fix versions ↔ releases" row to the sync-semantics table in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` (section "Sync semantics & limitations", line 321), marking inbound supported and outbound as delivered by the next child, and pointing to ADR 0123.

Imported tickets: the inbound CREATE path is unchanged. A ticket created from a Jira issue gets its releases on the following pass through the bound-ticket update diff, so no CREATE body change and no second CREATE writer.

Safety while only this direction exists: no local writer of `RELEASE_DELTA` exists until the surfaces child, so the inbound set-diff cannot strip a locally intended release. The surfaces child depends on the outbound child for that reason.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`
- `src/rebar/reconciler/inbound_collection_diffs.py`
- `src/rebar/reconciler/inbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/reconciler/run_differs.py`
- `src/rebar/reconciler/mutation_payloads.py`
- `src/rebar/reconciler/apply_inbound_events.py`
- `src/rebar/reconciler/apply_inbound.py`
- `src/rebar/reconciler/_field_contract.py`
- `src/rebar/reconciler/conflict_resolver.py`
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`
- `tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_releases.py` (new)
- `tests/unit/reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_apply_releases.py` (new)
- `tests/unit/reconciler/test_field_contract_properties.py` (extend)
- `tests/unit/reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_snapshot.py` (extend: Cloud field list)
- `tests/unit/reconciler/test_dc_backend_characterization.py` (extend: DC payload keeps `fixVersions`)

## Testing

Payload fixtures use the documented version object shape (`{"self","id","name","archived","released"}`, Jira Cloud OpenAPI `Version`), because no project on the production site has a version to record (ADR 0123 Evidence).
- Diff: Jira `[{"name":"2.4"},{"name":"2.5"}]` vs local `["2.4","old"]` yields add `2.5`, remove `old`; equal sets yield `[]`; `fixVersions` absent yields `[]` even when local has releases; a malformed entry (no name, non-dict) is skipped.
- Apply: an update mutation with release add/remove writes exactly one `RELEASE_DELTA` with `source="inbound"`; a repeat with the state already matching writes nothing; a reducer exception writes nothing; a mutation with both add and remove of one name writes it as added only. Existing label-apply tests pass unchanged (they pin the extraction).
- Cloud fetch requests `fixVersions`; a DC search payload carrying `fixVersions` reaches the snapshot with names intact.
- Contract: `FIELD_CONTRACT["releases"]` is `ADD_WINS`/`set`, and `process_release_delta` keeps a name both added and removed in one event (add-wins property, mirroring the labels property test).
- Two passes over the same Jira payload: the first writes one `RELEASE_DELTA`, the second writes nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A bound Jira issue whose `fixVersions` gain or lose a name produces one `RELEASE_DELTA` (`source="inbound"`) with that delta on the bound ticket, for both Cloud- and DC-shaped payloads; pinned by the tests above.
- [ ] A repeat pass with no Jira change writes no event, and a snapshot without the `fixVersions` key never removes local releases; pinned by tests.
- [ ] `FIELD_CONTRACT` and `conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES` both register `releases` (`ADD_WINS`, `set`), and `tests/unit/reconciler/test_field_contract_properties.py` passes with the new add-wins case.
- [ ] Existing label inbound tests in `tests/unit/reconciler/` pass unchanged.
- [ ] `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` lists the fix-versions row.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` and `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` both exit 0, and no `src/rebar` file exceeds 800 lines.
- [ ] `env -u JIRA_URL -u JIRA_USER -u JIRA_API_TOKEN make verify` exits 0 on the commit pushed for review.
data.title: Sync Jira fixVersions into rebar releases (inbound)
